summary: Teardown helper: walks a fixed table of 45 heap pointers anchored at byte_8AFC74 backwards at a 20-byte stride, freeing each non-null entry through FreeWrapper_7bcf, and returns the last processed pointer value (the last freed block, or null when no entry was non-null). Used in the pit/tire-wear property cleanup path.

operations.description: Seed the walk cursor v0 with the address of byte_8AFC74, the end anchor of a 45-entry pointer table.
Seed the iteration counter v1 with 45, the table entry count.
do-while loop that runs 45 times: v1 is decremented each iteration and the loop exits when v1 reaches zero.
Read the candidate pointer as the dword 20 bytes below the current cursor, *((_DWORD *)v0 - 5).
Step the cursor backward by the 20-byte table entry stride: v0 -= 20.
Only free the candidate when the read pointer is non-null.
Free the non-null heap block via FreeWrapper_7bcf(candidate) and store its result.
Return the last candidate value (the last freed pointer, or null if every entry was null).

clean_pseudocode: char *cursor = &byte_8AFC74;            // end anchor of the 45-entry table
result = *(unsigned int *)(cursor - 20);   // entry pointer 20 bytes below cursor
unresolved: The layout and element type of the 45-entry, 20-byte-stride table anchored at byte_8AFC74 are unknown; only the end-anchor address is evidenced.
The ABI label Tire_Wear_Property_Cleanup is legacy naming; the table's semantic role (tire-wear properties) is unproven by runtime evidence.
